$comment:
CANT-13, criterion 12. Every field of the wire schema, mapped to what backs it.

This file exists because the wire schema and the DDL have no mechanical relation, so "the generated schema and the migrations disagree" was undefined and a guard written against it could not fail — it could only be reinterpreted at verification time.

Three kinds:
  column       - read from or written to a database column. Names the table and column, and a json_path when the value lives inside a JSONB document.
  derived      - computed by the server at request time from other columns, from configuration, or from connection state. Never stored, so it cannot drift from what it summarises.
  client-local - the server has no opinion. Invariant 3: sending, queued and failed describe a message's relationship to its own outbox and are not expressible on the wire.

A required wire field backed by a nullable column must say why, in one of two ways.
  required_via     - names the CHECK constraint that makes it present anyway. This is how one
                     attachments table carries two kinds.
  nullable_because - states why the wire's requirement and the column's nullability are both correct.
                     Used where the wire field is required within an OPTIONAL parent, where the frame
                     is inbound and storage has other sources, or where the served value is derived
                     for some rows and stored for others.
Neither is a licence: the guard fails when a required field has a nullable column and says nothing.

The guard is internal/store/wiremap_test.go. Adding a field to the wire schema and not to this file fails the build.

User.name.note: Served live so a rename propagates; never frozen into a message row.

User.initials.note: Computed from display_name at serve time. Storing it would be a second source of truth that goes stale on a rename.

Transcript.state.note: Required on VoiceAttachment: without it the server cannot serve a voice note at all, not even a pending one.

Transcript.text.note: Authoritative per ATTACHMENT, because Transcript hangs off VoiceAttachment and a message may carry more than one voice note. messages.transcript_text is a denormalised copy of this for CANT-59's single to_tsvector index and is never read to serve a message — a per-message column cannot hold two transcripts, and the second job to write it would silently replace the first.

Transcript.eta_sec.note: The schema forbids the client to invent this, so it is the ASR job's value or absent.

VoiceAttachment.url.note: Derived at serve time from attachments.storage_key. NOT stored: the wire says it may be presigned and time-limited, so whether it is an R2 GET or a Traefik route is CANT-47's decision and a stored URL is wrong the moment that lands.

VoiceAttachment.peaks.note: Computed server-side: the seeded generator overflows 2^53 and produces different bars in JavaScript than in Dart.

ImageAttachment.url.note: Derived at serve time from attachments.storage_key, as VoiceAttachment.url.

ImageAttachment.placeholder.note: The blurhash, computed server-side on ingest.

ReplyRef.message_id.note: The ref itself is the stored half; every other ReplyRef field is read off the source message at serve time.
ReplyRef.message_id.nullable_because: Required WITHIN a ReplyRef, and Message.reply_to is itself optional — so the column is null exactly when there is no ref to serve. Also null after CANT-67 sweeps the source, which is why the FK is ON DELETE SET NULL.

ReplyRef.author_id.note: Read from the source message's author_id. Not copied, so an edit or a rename is reflected.

ReplyRef.kind.note: Read from the source message's text and attachments.

ReplyRef.preview.note: Read from the source message's text or transcript at serve time.

ReplyRef.duration_ms.note: Read from the source message's voice attachment.

ReplyRef.url.note: Derived from the source attachment's storage_key.

Message.seq.note: Dense per conversation; drawn from conversations.last_seq in the inserting transaction.

Message.log_seq.note: Server-global and sparse; drawn from log_counter's single row in the same transaction.

Message.attachments.note: Composed from the attachments rows for this message, ordered by position.

Message.reply_to.note: Composed from ReplyRef's own mappings; NULL after CANT-67 sweeps the source.

Message.state.note: Per-reader delivery state. Not stored: it is a function of the reader, so a column would have to be per reader per message. CANT-90: the SUBJECT changes with authorship — on someone else's message it describes the reader (`delivered` served, `read` once their read_seq passed it); on the reader's own it describes everyone else (`sent`, then `read` once Message.read_by exceeds 1, never `delivered`). Derived from the same count read_by is served from, so the word and the number cannot disagree.

Message.read_by.note: Count over conversation_members.read_seq, PLUS THE AUTHOR, who counts by derivation rather than by a receipt — sending does not advance read_seq (0005). Not stored, so it cannot drift from the receipts it summarises, and it counts the same population member_count does, so the fraction can reach n/n. CANT-26.

Message.edited_at.note: Column present; what an edit MEANS is CANT-63's.

Message.deleted.note: Column present; what a delete MEANS is CANT-63's.

Conversation.kind.note: Mutable: a third member promotes a direct to a group.

Conversation.name.note: NULL for a direct — the rail shows the other member, which is per reader. `name` is REQUIRED on the wire, so for kind=direct the served value is RESOLVED from the other member's display_name at serve time (CANT-20). A group reads the column.
Conversation.name.nullable_because: The wire makes name REQUIRED and the column is nullable, and both are right: a group's name is this column, and a direct has none, because the rail shows the OTHER member and that is per reader. The server derives the served name for a direct rather than storing one — storing it would freeze a display name that SyncResponse.users exists to serve live.

Conversation.member_count.note: Count over conversation_members. Not stored: that table already answers it.

Conversation.muted.note: Per reader, so it lives on the membership rather than the conversation.

Conversation.first_unread_seq.note: The first seq above conversation_members.read_seq that the VIEWER DID NOT AUTHOR; absent when there is none. An index scan over UNIQUE (conversation_id, seq), not a table scan. read_seq is advanced by CANT-26's read receipts and by nothing else — an author's own send does NOT advance it, and the author filter is what keeps your own messages out of your own unread count. CANT-83 implemented the advance and removed it; see migrations/0005_read_seq_derivation.

Conversation.head_seq.note: Served from conversations.last_seq. NOT a column: with the row lock the bump and the insert commit together, so the two would be one number stored twice.

Conversation.retention_days.note: NULL means inherit the global infinite default, not zero days.

SyncResponse.log_seq.note: The caller's new HIGH-WATER MARK, which is the server's log_counter value at read time ONLY when has_more is false. With has_more true it is the last message actually returned, because nothing beyond that was scanned and claiming the head would skip whatever sits between. Both halves come from the schema: "not the server's head, which may be further along when has_more is true", and "deriving this client-side by maxing over messages is wrong the moment a page contains no messages the client can see". CANT-20 implements it; an earlier note here said only the head, which is the half that is wrong.

SyncResponse.messages.note: The page of messages after the client's cursor.

SyncResponse.conversations.note: The conversations referenced by this page, so a client can render one it has never seen.

SyncResponse.users.note: The users referenced by this page. Served live rather than frozen into messages, which is why a rename propagates.

SyncResponse.has_more.note: Whether the page hit its limit.

ClientHello.type.note: The union discriminator. Set by the codec, never stored.

ServerReady.type.note: The union discriminator. Set by the codec, never stored.

Ping.type.note: The union discriminator. Set by the codec, never stored.

Pong.type.note: The union discriminator. Set by the codec, never stored.

ClientSend.type.note: The union discriminator. Set by the codec, never stored.

ServerAck.type.note: The union discriminator. Set by the codec, never stored.

ServerMessageFrame.type.note: The union discriminator. Set by the codec, never stored.

ServerReceipt.type.note: The union discriminator. Set by the codec, never stored.

ClientRead.type.note: The union discriminator. Set by the codec, never stored.

ClientTyping.type.note: The union discriminator. Set by the codec, never stored.

ServerTyping.type.note: The union discriminator. Set by the codec, never stored.

ServerError.type.note: The union discriminator. Set by the codec, never stored.

ServerResyncRequired.type.note: The union discriminator. Set by the codec, never stored.

ClientHello.wire_version.note: Compared against the server's wire_version at handshake; CANT-74 owns the policy. Not stored.

ClientHello.device_id.note: Resolved against devices.id at handshake and checked for devices.revoked_at. Not stored by the handshake itself; the device row already exists.

ClientHello.resume_from_log_seq.note: The client's cursor, held for the life of the connection. CANT-24.

ServerReady.heartbeat_interval_sec.note: Server-driven dial from config. R1 measured the cost of the value: at 35 s a client can believe it is connected for 70-105 s after it is not.

ServerReady.log_seq.note: The server's current log_counter value at accept.

ServerReady.resumed.note: Whether the cursor was honoured or the client must /sync. CANT-24.

Ping.id.note: Correlation id for one heartbeat exchange. Never stored.

OutboundAttachment.kind.note: Names which upload is being attached; the stored kind is attachments.kind, written by ingest.

OutboundAttachment.upload_id.note: Resolved against the pending upload at send time. CANT-48 owns the upload record.

ClientSend.client_id.note: Inbound: the idempotency key, checked BEFORE either ordinal is drawn and then stored.
ClientSend.client_id.nullable_because: Required on the inbound frame — a client that omits it forfeits deduplication — but nullable in storage, and the honest reason is narrower than it looks: NOTHING WRITES NULL TODAY. Every sending surface supplies a key, bots included — CANT-75's REST send takes client_id in its body and its Done-when requires that a sender with no device row is deduplicated exactly like one with, which is the case that matters most because a cron-driven bot retries mechanically and may run as two replicas. store.SendMessage refuses the zero value outright (CANT-14). The column is nullable as deliberate headroom for a genuinely server-originated row, should one ever exist; Postgres treating such NULLs as distinct would be correct, because they would never have been deduplicated. An earlier draft of this note claimed bots have no client_id — that was contradicted by CANT-75 and is corrected here (CANT-77).

ClientSend.attachments.note: Resolved to attachments rows by ingest; see OutboundAttachment.

ServerAck.client_id.note: Echoed from the send it acknowledges.

ServerAck.message_id.note: The id of the row that was inserted, or of the original on a duplicate.

ServerAck.seq.note: The seq that was drawn, read back from the inserted row.

ServerAck.duplicate.note: True when the idempotency check hit. Not a column: it describes this request, not the message.

ServerReceipt.conversation_id.note: Echoed from the read that caused it.

ServerReceipt.up_to_seq.note: The receipt is the fanout of this write.

ClientRead.conversation_id.note: Names the membership row to advance.

ClientTyping.conversation_id.note: Typing is connection state, never stored. CANT-64.

ClientTyping.state.note: Typing is ephemeral per connection. The server fans it out and keeps nothing; a restart forgets every typing indicator, which is correct.

ServerTyping.user_ids.note: Held in connection state for the debounce window. CANT-64.

ServerError.retryable.note: Whether the client should try again.

ServerError.client_id.note: Echoed when the error is about a specific send, so an outbox entry can be resolved.

ServerResyncRequired.reason.note: Why the cursor could not be honoured. CANT-24.

ServerResyncRequired.log_seq.note: The cursor the client should sync from instead.

EnrolRequest.enrolment_token.note: PRESENTED OR RETURNED, NEVER STORED. enrolment_tokens.token_hash holds this string's SHA-256 and nothing anywhere holds the string: it exists in the one message that carried it and is unrecoverable afterwards. Mapping it to a column would be a claim that the database keeps a working credential, which is exactly what hashing it is for.

EnrolRequest.device_name.note: What the device list calls this install. Required rather than defaulted, because a revocation list is unusable if the rows do not say which phone they are.

EnrolResponse.user_id.note: Learned here because a client needs it before its first page: author_id is the only thing separating a message you wrote from one you did not, and every read-state rule turns on that.

EnrolResponse.device_id.note: Minted by the redemption. It is what ClientHello.device_id carries and what a revocation names.

EnrolResponse.access_token.note: PRESENTED OR RETURNED, NEVER STORED. access_tokens.token_hash holds this string's SHA-256 and nothing anywhere holds the string: it exists in the one message that carried it and is unrecoverable afterwards. Mapping it to a column would be a claim that the database keeps a working credential, which is exactly what hashing it is for.

EnrolResponse.access_expires_at.note: Served so a client never hard-codes the lifetime — the way the two drift apart the first time it changes.
EnrolResponse.access_expires_at.nullable_because: NULL in the column means NEVER EXPIRES, and 0007's CHECK ties that to a NULL device_id, so only a bot's token can hold one. A bot has no enrolment and no refresh, so it never reaches this response: every row this field is served from has a device and therefore an expiry.

EnrolResponse.refresh_token.note: PRESENTED OR RETURNED, NEVER STORED. refresh_tokens.token_hash holds this string's SHA-256 and nothing anywhere holds the string: it exists in the one message that carried it and is unrecoverable afterwards. Mapping it to a column would be a claim that the database keeps a working credential, which is exactly what hashing it is for.

EnrolResponse.refresh_expires_at.note: Sixty days, so a phone in normal use never re-authenticates and one left in a drawer falls out of the account on its own.
